summary: Crowded on both sides: runtime CSPM is consolidating into well-funded platforms that will add IaC scanning, and the IaC scanner wedge is already free (cfn_nag, tfsec, conftest/OPA, HashiCorp Sentinel). The open gap is unifying code and runtime with fixes as PRs, but that lead is likely only 12-18 months before a platform copies or acquires it.

objections.objection: The free IaC scanner wedge is already commoditised. cfn_nag (MIT, around since 2016) lints CloudFormation for open security groups, wildcard IAM and missing encryption; tfsec (MIT) does the same for Terraform; conftest runs OPA policies over Terraform. The concept's OSS scanner adds nothing new, so community adoption has to be won against tools engineers already run.

HashiCorp owns the Terraform workflow and already sells Sentinel policy as code. It runs between plan and apply in Terraform Cloud/Enterprise, which is exactly the concept's pre-deployment checkpoint. HashiCorp could ship a library of security policies next quarter and sell it bundled to the same platform teams. The concept's competitor table doesn't mention HashiCorp at all.

Most dangerous competitor: the consolidating CSPM platforms, above all Palo Alto Networks, which bought RedLock and Evident.io in 2018, plus Check Point/Dome9. They already have CISO relationships, compliance mapping and runtime scanning across clouds. All they lack is IaC scanning, which they can bolt on or acquire. The concept's top-down CISO sale meets them head-on.

Cloud providers bundle posture checks: AWS Config rules and Security Hub CIS checks, Azure Security Center, GCP Security Command Center. Bundling caps how much buyers will pay for the runtime-scan and CIS-mapping features, and $10 per resource per month looks high against them.

Developer-first security vendors with distribution in pull requests, Snyk above all, can extend into IaC configuration. Snyk is listed as a differentiator, but it is really a fast follower with the same bottom-up motion and an existing installed base.

Other dedicated cloud-governance startups (DivvyCloud, Fugue, CloudCheckr, Accurics/Terrascan-type IaC entrants) are missing from the table. That understates how crowded the field is and how hard the market will be to explain.

strongest_point: No incumbent unified IaC and runtime under one policy set with fixes as pull requests. Runtime CSPM consoles target security teams, which leaves a real developer-workflow opening.
what_would_change_my_mind: The OSS scanner beats cfn_nag/tfsec on adoption (more GitHub stars and CI installs within 6 months).
Design partners who already run Prisma/Dome9 or Sentinel say they would add or switch for code-to-runtime mapping and PR fixes.
A remediation PR success rate above 80% that incumbents cannot show.
